input.prospect_context: Startup is behind on hiring but worried about offshore access controls.
input.signal_brief: Two backend roles and one data role remain unfilled after funding round.
input.bench_context: Tenacious can work with access controls and named engineers.
input.prior_thread: Prospect asks for a fast proposal but has not confirmed security constraints.

candidate_output: The unfilled backend and data roles suggest there may be a delivery gap, but I would not send a proposal before understanding the access-control constraints. The right next step is a short security and delivery scoping call so we can decide whether a named-engineer squad is actually appropriate.

input.prospect_context: Company cut costs but needs roadmap continuity.
input.signal_brief: Investor letter emphasized cost discipline after layoffs.
input.bench_context: Tenacious can provide optional monthly engagement structure.
input.prior_thread: Prospect asks whether this will lock them into a long contract.

candidate_output: Given the cost-discipline context after layoffs, flexibility matters. Our standard structure would avoid a long lock-in: monthly engagement with short extension blocks. Before pricing anything, I would want to scope the exact delivery lane that needs continuity.

input.prospect_context: New CTO is skeptical because previous outsourcing failed.
input.signal_brief: Previous vendor added management layers and slowed delivery.
input.bench_context: Tenacious favors direct engineer participation in Slack, standups, and code review.
input.prior_thread: Prospect asks what would be different.

candidate_output: The management-layer problem is a real failure mode. The difference I would test is whether direct engineer participation in your Slack, standups, and code review reduces that translation loss. I would not ask you to take that on faith; a scoped technical conversation is the next step.

input.prospect_context: Buyer asks whether Tenacious can build an agentic recommendation system.
input.signal_brief: Data-science lead is skeptical of agentic architecture.
input.bench_context: Tenacious should frame evaluation honestly and avoid false certainty.
input.prior_thread: Prospect asks if the model will beat their embedding baseline.

candidate_output: I would not claim it will beat the embedding baseline before testing. Since your data-science lead is skeptical, the right deliverable is a prototype evaluated against the metric your team trusts. One valid outcome is that the agentic approach does not beat the baseline, and we should say that clearly if it happens.
